diagnosis.reason: Full positive-pool documents and checked canonical native records show lettering and sign-adjacent material, but no inspected option combines a specified character sequence with actual carrier attachment and local physical placement for everyday scene text. Baseline top8 contains no fitting scene inscription; it exposes physical openings, glass smudges and print artifacts. Existing shirt/artifact lettering is owner-specific rather than transferable. This is a bounded inventory finding, not a proof that every language variant in the corpus is absent. The five fixed-literal examples contribute diverse scene-text relations but cannot satisfy a different frozen word; one additional declaration-preserving relation addresses that compatibility gap without naming the probe word.

existing_candidates.meaning: A faint smudge remains near the glass pull while the rest of the pane keeps its reflection and transparency.
existing_candidates.limitation: Baseline rank 3; surface attachment is useful, but a smudge is not an inscription, has no spelling, and declares material effects only.
Physical sign object and wetness are specified; characters, their sequence, legibility and precise placement are absent.
A lighting effect cannot establish readable text; original sci-fi/night/cyberpunk/stage/performance applicability remains binding.

existing_candidates.meaning: a continuous bent glass tube forms a sign stroke; the visible luminous region lies inside that tube; end electrodes and feed wires belong to that stroke
existing_candidates.limitation: Strong apparatus ownership but no literal character sequence. Luminosity alone cannot witness inscription spelling.

existing_candidates.meaning: a short line of display lettering is arranged as the main graphic on the T-shirt front
existing_candidates.limitation: A real lettering/carrier relation exists, but its owner is tee front lettering. Moving it to door glass would discard its declared owner; no exact content is supplied.
Identifies a handwritten object without words or layout; human applicability is intrinsic, so it cannot silently become an unrestricted text candidate.

existing_candidates.meaning: POV-style caption context reading as “you caught me” intimacy
existing_candidates.limitation: Publication interpretation with human applicability; no physical in-scene carrier. Its text dimension does not make it direct visible lettering.

existing_candidates.meaning: A readable caption panel occupies a bounded lower picture region, distinct from its backing field and preserving focal evidence above it.
existing_candidates.limitation: Declared owner is displayed artwork/picture region, with independent profile activation. A graphic caption panel cannot substitute for paint on a real entrance door.

research_sources.title: NPS Preservation Brief 25: The Preservation of Historic Signs
research_sources.supports: Documents physical sign carriers including doors, window glass, wall surfaces and hanging boards, plus illuminated lettering. Historical practice supports the carrier relations; the authored examples are new illustrative scenes.

research_sources.title: U.S. Access Board: Chapter 7 Signs
research_sources.supports: Distinguishes character form, contrast, finish, spacing and viewing distance as factors relevant to legibility. This is accessibility guidance for covered signs, not a universal photographic prescription or compliance assertion.

research_sources.title: IPTC Photo Metadata User Guide
research_sources.supports: Explains Description/Caption as information about the photograph, often displayed below it. That contextual metadata does not establish physically depicted lettering.

research_sources.title: ICDAR Robust Reading Competition: Incidental Scene Text Tasks
research_sources.supports: Separates locating text regions from recognizing their character content. This supports treating placement and transcription as distinct evidence requirements.

inventory_method.method: Inspected full global document text without tag prefilter, then loaded exact records through checked BodyReader and installed photo_canonical_source.native. Compared selected working V3 content against decoded canonical V4 meaning. Pattern discovery was a navigation aid, not exhaustive semantic absence proof.
inventory_method.working_comparison: Inspected working source for the glass-smudge, wet-neon, sign-spill, recipe-card and slogan-shirt CIDs; selected meanings and intrinsic guards agree with decoded installed records.

top1.meaning: Physical foreground opening encloses the subject with depth evidence.
top1.limitation: An opening is a spatial boundary, not the word OPEN.

top3.meaning: Local smudge near glass door pull.

confusion_boundaries: The letters O-P-E-N name a character sequence; an open door or operating-hours inference cannot supply that sequence. None of the additions inserts the known probe word.
A sign object, letter-like light, luminous color spill or blurred stroke is insufficient to establish its exact readable wording.
Text needs both transcription and scene location: carrier, attachment and local placement. Reading a word elsewhere in the frame does not preserve these relationships.

Publication captions, metadata and lower-third graphics do not establish physical inscriptions on objects in the photographed space. A photographed printed artifact remains a separate declared carrier.
Material, numeral, script or lettering style alone cannot establish a business identity, current operating state, real address, contents, historical date or legal compliance.

Exact case, punctuation and line breaks are meaningful when specified; a recognized concept or translated word does not preserve literal spelling. Readability must ultimately be inspected in saved pixels at relevant size.
recommendations: Integrate only these six bounded drafts through normal source/native review. Five are fixed-literal examples; the sixth preserves existing declared text under complete application prerequisites. All remain discovery-only until qualified.
Preserve the original probe bytes for before/after evaluation. Report retrieval exposure separately from meaning compatibility, native review and saved-image text fidelity.

Keep full carrier and spelling semantics if an option is adopted; adapting distinctive wording or medium requires actual authorial review under the existing workflow, not a silent transfer of shirt/artwork ownership.

For the five illustrative scenes, review all object/material/light/setting effects. The sixth introduces no object or wording and declares text presentation effects only: its carrier, medium, exact inscription and local placement must already be established. Check its four native guard prerequisites plus the complete application contract; guard syntax validation alone does not establish nonempty exact transcription.
Do not infer a render guarantee from a well-formed candidate. Exact transcription, orientation, carrier and placement need separate pixel inspection if images are later generated.

status: Six drafts ready for parent integration review, including one general declaration-preserving carrier relation. No operating corpus, index, CURRENT, runtime, code, commit or image changed.

fixed_literal_examples.role_contribution: Actual scene lettering with complete carrier and placement relations.
fixed_literal_examples.exact_text_compatibility: Each prescribes its authored literal content. All five are incompatible with a frozen inscription that differs; they must not be silently substituted or treated as exact-query successes.

general_relation.role_contribution: Makes the same predeclared painted inscription readable as attached to its predeclared door-glass carrier and local placement.
general_relation.exact_text_compatibility: Potentially compatible with arbitrary independently declared inscription content because it supplies no new literal. Compatibility requires confirming every application prerequisite, full source meaning, actual owner selection and text-preservation scope.
general_relation.native_limit: The current source-guard vocabulary has exact scalar and frozen entity-relation predicates, but no arbitrary nonempty-transcription predicate. Its preservation scopes cover reference_appearance/requester_identity, not text. The four guards are real prerequisites, not full authority for the generic transcription requirement. Complete exact text and local placement declarations require independent semantic review; no source proof or native eligibility is claimed. Missing declarations remain review-required and cannot be inferred from the role name.
